Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB192.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Daxiu Zhu. Daxiu Zhu owns the retained deployment, ruling the porridge and rice, the walking and sitting, each stirring and stillness all not in the bowl of the world, with Bodhidharma as fellow traveler for the one who knows.

Senses.Explanation: A paired unit naming each stirring and each stillness of the day, listed beside its sibling pairs and ruled on wherever the records locate the working. Ying'an Tanhua rules that to say the thus-come one is seen in the twelve double-hours' each stirring and stillness, word and silence, turn and bow is taking the thief for a son — and to say he is not discerned there is madness running outward; Mi'an Xianjie strings the pairs on the hall seat — one advance one retreat, one stirring one stillness, trust the naga ever in composure — with one seize one release, one kill one quicken, the Jiazhou elephant salt-heavy and the Shanfu iron bull thirsty; Wuzhun Shifan, before the assembly, holds that once the shapes of stirring and stillness cannot be found, each stirring and stillness, exit and entry, release and gather, advance and retreat is nowhere other than the playground of the uncanny light and freedom; and Cishou Huaishen, taking leave of the assembly, likens it to the wild crane's wheeling and the floating clouds' gathering and scattering — no north or south, no coming or going, the wayfarer's heart just so. Tianru Weize runs his own day before the assembly — rising, washing, porridge, sweeping leaves, watching the fish, one word one silence, one stirring one stillness — hawking the assembly's life-lord without pause through the six watches of day and night; Qianyan Yuanzhang ties it to the one sentence: today's doing clear, then each stirring and stillness, word and silence, rise and fall, birth and death — living just so, dying just so; Guting Shanjian hatches his bird on it — brooding without losing the clutch through stirring and stillness until the shell falls apart and the lively one hops out knowing hunger and fullness, feathers whole, flying where it will; and Daxiu Zhu, reversing Gaofeng Yuanmiao's bowl of the world, rules the porridge and rice, the dung and water, the walking and sitting, each stirring and stillness all not in it — know that and Bodhidharma becomes one's fellow traveler; miss it and one boils tea with water and cooks rice with rice.
